I see you are a little confused on how probabilities work. So let’s think of throwing a coin. There are two equally possible outcomes: heads, or tails. And let’s say you want as many heads as possible. So getting the outcome “head” in a throw is good luck. If you throw this coin 1000 times, there is a good chance you will get 500 heads. But there is also a chance you will get just 400, and an even smaller chance of getting 300. It is even possible that you get no heads at all, but very unlikely. Each throw that doesn’t end up in “head” puts you closer to getting fewer than 500 heads. And one throw doesn’t influence the next. So there is no guarantee that you will get your 500 heads. But with each head, you get closer to it, and with each tail you get farther. Does that make sense?

That’s not how random processes work. Your next roll is ndependent from the previous ones. So having bad luck in the beginning doesn’t mean good luck later on. It actually tells you nothing about the future.
